Innovation.name: Creative Problem-Solving
Innovation.stem: Many people abandon your team's intake/onboarding process partway through; the standard fix is to add staff. MOST / LEAST:

options.A: Add more staff to move people through faster.
options.B: Map where people drop off and redesign those steps, piloting a simpler flow.
options.D: Copy another team's process wholesale without testing fit.

Results Oriented.name: Outcome Ownership
Results Oriented.stem: Mid-period, your team is behind a key target due to a supplier delay. MOST / LEAST:

options.A: Report the supplier as the reason and lower expectations.
options.B: Re-plan with the team to recover what's achievable while escalating the supplier issue in parallel.
options.C: Push the team harder without changing the plan.
options.D: Wait to see if the supplier recovers on its own.

Effective Collaboration and Communicatio.name: Cross-Functional Collaboration
Effective Collaboration and Communicatio.stem: Your goals conflict with another unit's, yet both are needed for the outcome. MOST / LEAST:

options.A: Optimise your own unit's metric and let them manage theirs.
options.B: Align on the shared outcome and negotiate the trade-offs jointly.

Professionalism and Integrity.name: Ethical Conduct
Professionalism and Integrity.stem: A top performer is bending an important rule or standard to hit targets. MOST / LEAST:

options.A: Ignore it because of their results.
options.B: Address it directly, uphold the standard, and escalate per policy.
options.C: Hint that they should be careful, but take no real action.
options.D: Apply the rule to others but not to them.

Accountability & Ownership.name: Accountability for Commitments
Accountability & Ownership.stem: You realise you'll miss a deadline you promised a colleague. MOST / LEAST:

options.A: Say nothing and hope they don't notice.
options.B: Tell them as soon as you know, with a revised date and a plan.

Strategic Mindset.name: Forward Strategy Setting
Strategic Mindset.stem: You lead a team. A competitor's new approach is winning over younger customers, and an industry shift is expected within ~18 months. Leadership wants this quarter's targets protected. MOST / LEAST effective:

options.A: Keep the team focused on this quarter's targets; revisit the threat next year.
options.B: Run a scenario analysis of the shift and shape a 2–3 year response **while** protecting near-term targets.
options.C: Immediately divert investment into an untested new offering.
options.D: Wait for competitors to move, then copy the winning approach.

Drives Sustainable Performance.name: Resource Mobilisation
Drives Sustainable Performance.stem: You're handed a priority project with no extra budget or people. MOST / LEAST:

options.A: Decline, citing a lack of resources.
options.B: Identify and negotiate for the critical resources, repurpose what you have, and sequence smartly.
options.C: Proceed with nothing and hope it works out.
options.D: Quietly pull people off other work without telling anyone.

Makes Effective Decisions and Plans.name: Sound Judgement
Makes Effective Decisions and Plans.stem: A possible serious problem appears in an important account or process. Confirming it will take ~48 hours; acting now may harm a key relationship; doing nothing risks a major breach. MOST / LEAST:

options.A: Wait for full confirmation to avoid friction.
options.B: Apply targeted, proportionate interim measures while expediting the check and informing the right people.
options.C: Take the most drastic action immediately.
options.D: Flag it but take no interim action.

Inspires & Motivates.name: Mobilising Around Purpose
Inspires & Motivates.stem: Your team is demoralised during a reorganisation. MOST / LEAST:

options.A: Tell them to focus on their tasks and stop worrying.
options.B: Connect their work to a clear, credible picture of where the unit is heading and why it matters.
options.C: Promise everything will be fine, without basis.
options.D: Vent your own frustration openly to bond with them.

Leads by Example.name: Trust & Credibility
Leads by Example.stem: You made a commitment to a peer, but circumstances changed. MOST / LEAST:

options.A: Quietly drop it and hope it's forgotten.
options.B: Proactively tell them, explain honestly, and propose how to make good.
options.C: Deliver something half-done to technically comply.
options.D: Deny you ever committed to it.
